panels.rationale: Single-image barium swallow radiograph from a case report of Allgrove syndrome in a child. The caption and in-text mention describe achalasia with lower esophageal sphincter narrowing and esophageal body dilatation (bird's beak sign), matching the configured Allgrove syndrome manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: Salame et al. Allgrove syndrome with early neurodegeneration in a child: A case report from Syria.. Medicine 2026. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000047238. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Barium swallow test showing narrowing of the lower esophageal sphincter as well as dilatation of the esophagus body (bird’s beak sign).
in_text_mentions: Further investigations, including a barium swallow test, revealed stenosis of the lower esophageal sphincter and complete body dilatation of the esophagus (bird beak sign), leading to a diagnosis of achalasia (Fig. 1). Treatment with nifedipine was initiated, and surgery was postponed until the child’s medical condition allowed her to undergo surgery. Subsequently, the patient was discharged. On follow-up, her ACTH laboratory value was normal (28 pg/mL).

panels.rationale: Single-panel barium swallow radiograph from a case report of Triple A (Allgrove) syndrome showing a dilated, tortuous esophagus with arrows marking the outline and a narrowed distal segment, matching the captioned manifestation of esophageal dilatation/achalasia listed in the vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Anderle et al. Triple A syndrome with a new mutation pattern, first documented case in Austria: a case report with literature review.. Orphanet journal of rare diseases 2026. doi:10.1186/s13023-026-04465-5. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Barium swallow radiograph demonstrating a dilated and tortuous oesophagus (arrows)
in_text_mentions: A barium swallow test showed dilation of the proximal oesophagus, narrowing of the distal end and tertiary contractures (Fig. 1), which were then successfully treated with endoscopic dilation. The patient was under glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement therapy due to adrenal insufficiency since the age of seven. His plasma ACTH, renin, serum electrolyte, and aldosterone levels were found to be within normal ranges. Upon taking the medical history, dysarthria was noticeable. The patient reported the absence of tears since early childhood, which was confirmed by the Schirmer test.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Coronal brain MRI from a child with Allgrove syndrome showing captioned cortical atrophy; this is a neurodegenerative manifestation but not represented in the provided finding vocabulary. B: Sagittal brain MRI from a child with Allgrove syndrome showing captioned cerebellar atrophy, corpus callosum thinning, and mega cisterna magna; findings are not in the provided vocabulary. C: Axial MRI with arrows marking bilateral lacrimal gland atrophy, supporting the alacrima component of Allgrove syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Salame et al. Allgrove syndrome with early neurodegeneration in a child: A case report from Syria.. Medicine 2026. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000047238. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: MRI revealing (A) cortical atrophy in the cerebrum, (B) cerebellar atrophy, thinning of the corpus callosum, mega cisterna magna, and (C) bilateral atrophy of lacrimal glands (arrows). MRI = magnetic resonance imaging.
in_text_mentions: esponsive to speech. Random and involuntary movements of the head and limb were observed. Hypertonia of the lower extremities and hyperreflexia (+3 on both sides) were noted. Lumbar puncture revealed a normal cell count. MRI revealed cortical atrophy with high signal intensity in the periventricular white matter, cerebellar atrophy, thinning of the corpus callosum, and a mega cisterna magna. Furthermore, atrophy of the lacrimal glands on both sides was observed (Fig. 2). For additional evaluation, electroencephalography showed a consistent abnormal pattern with generalized discharges (Fig. 3).

in_text_mentions: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy showed a markedly dilated esophagus with retained food material and increased resistance at the lower esophageal sphincter. A barium swallow demonstrated the classic “bird’s beak” appearance with tapering at the gastroesophageal junction (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of both hands showing marked melanoderma, explicitly captioned and linked in the text to diffuse cutaneous hyperpigmentation in a patient with Allgrove syndrome. The panel is a real patient image and directly supports the Allgrove hyperpigmentation finding.
panels.attribution_text: Maizi et al. Allgrove Syndrome in Adults: A Case of an Atypical Presentation.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.98638. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: On physical examination, blood pressure measurements were within the normal range, and her body mass index (BMI) was 16.9 kg/m². She appeared clinically dehydrated and exhibited diffuse cutaneous and mucosal hyperpigmentation, particularly in the skin folds (Figure 1).
